title: New Zealand visitor recovery reaches near-pre-pandemic spend while travel purpose and market composition shift
source_unit: New Zealand Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment International Visitor Survey, year ending June 2026 release
geography: New Zealand; international visitors aged 15+ excluding foreign-fee-paying students, with market and travel-purpose breakdowns

observations.period: Year ending June 2026 compared with year ending June 2019; international visitor recovery

denominator.unit: International Visitor Survey achieved sample for the 2025/26 financial year; annual target 8,900

visitor_arrivals_vs_2019.unit: percent of year-ending-June-2019 international visitor arrivals

real_visitor_spend_vs_2019.unit: percent of year-ending-June-2019 international visitor expenditure after inflation adjustment

visitor_count.unit: million international visitors in the year ending June 2026

mechanism.value: Visitor volumes and real spend can recover at different speeds; near-recovery of spend does not imply equal regional dispersal, local benefit, or cultural-sector value capture

observations.method: MBIE International Visitor Survey rolling annual estimates, with visitor expenditure adjusted for inflation when compared with 2019; the survey measures expenditure, characteristics, behaviours, activities, satisfaction, transport, accommodation, and cultural experiences.
observations.uncertainty: The survey is designed for national estimates; regional expenditure breakdowns are not produced. Annual market estimates have different relative margins of error, and the 2024 series was recalibrated using a revised weighting approach affecting comparability, especially for China and Rest of Asia.
observations.subgroup: International visitors aged 15+ to New Zealand, excluding foreign-fee-paying students; market-level annual estimates include Australia, UK, USA, Rest of Europe, Asia, Germany, Canada, Rest of World, and China.
observations.counterinterpretation: Real spend near 2019 can reflect prices, visitor composition, length of stay, and high-spending segments rather than broad-based recovery in visitor access or local cultural economies.

observations.period: Year ending June 2026 compared with 2019; stated purpose of international visit

denominator.unit: International Visitor Survey annual sample frame; purpose shares are visitor-level weighted estimates

holiday_vacation_purpose.unit: percent of international visitors whose purpose was holiday/vacation

holiday_vacation_2019.unit: percent of international visitors whose purpose was holiday/vacation in 2019

visiting_friends_relatives_change.unit: percentage-point increase in visiting-friends-and-relatives share from 2019

market_recovery.value: Australia and USA visitor volumes each reached 105% of their 2019 levels; China and Rest of Asia estimates were affected by recalibration of earlier published expenditure attribution

mechanism.value: Tourism recovery is not a single demand type: holiday, visiting-friends/relatives, and market-specific flows imply different accommodation, mobility, cultural, and local-spending pathways

observations.method: Descriptive extraction from MBIE IVS year-ending-June-2026 release materials, using weighted visitor purpose and market estimates.
observations.uncertainty: Purpose is self-reported and visitor-level; it does not measure trip quality, cultural attendance, local spending distribution, or whether purpose changes are permanent. Comparisons inherit survey redesign, post-pandemic travel-pattern, and weighting limitations.
observations.subgroup: International visitors by stated travel purpose and country/region of residence.
observations.counterinterpretation: A higher holiday share can coexist with shorter stays, concentrated itineraries, high prices, or lower regional dispersal; visiting friends and relatives may shift expenditure toward households rather than formal tourism providers.

observations.period: June 2026 quarter and year ending June 2026; survey quality and cultural/visitor-experience scope

denominator.unit: June 2026 quarter achieved sample; annual and quarterly estimates have separate precision

annual_relative_margin_of_error_total.unit: percent relative margin of error for total year-ending-June-2026 estimate

quarterly_response_rate.unit: percent response rate for the June 2026 quarter

quarterly_total_relative_margin_of_error.unit: percent relative margin of error for total June 2026 quarter estimate

cultural_experience_scope.value: The release includes measures for Māori cultural experiences, visitor satisfaction, environment perceptions, activities, transport, accommodation, and product spend

mechanism.value: Visitor recovery can be evaluated through spending, cultural experience, satisfaction, environment, and mobility measures rather than arrivals alone, but quarterly precision limits fine-grained inference

observations.method: MBIE IVS quality and release-material documentation for annual and June-quarter 2026 estimates.
observations.uncertainty: Quarterly estimates have materially higher error than annual estimates; cultural-experience measures are survey responses and do not establish provider revenue, Māori community benefit, cultural authenticity, or durable learning.
observations.subgroup: International visitors surveyed in the June 2026 quarter and year-ending annual sample.
observations.counterinterpretation: A high satisfaction or cultural-experience response can coexist with uneven access, environmental pressure, or concentrated tourism benefits; survey quality metrics do not resolve those distributional questions.

related_sources.claim: MBIE IVS purpose, scope, methodology, recalibration, and release navigation.
Year-ending June 2026 recovery, visitor purpose, market, cultural-experience, and spend findings.
Annual and quarterly sample sizes, response rates, relative margins of error, and quality cautions.

boundary: This record adds an international mobility, visitor-spend, purpose, and cultural-experience layer. It does not establish household consumer trends, regional distribution of tourism benefits, local cultural-sector income, visitor causality, environmental impact, or Māori community outcomes.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: MBIE IVS release materials and survey-quality pages reviewed for year-ending June 2026 arrivals, inflation-adjusted spend recovery, purpose mix, market recovery, cultural-experience scope, sample size, response rate, margins of error, and recalibration limits.
